filename: Using machine learning to generate a GISS ModelE calibrated physics ensemble (CPE).pdf
title: Using Machine Learning to Generate a GISS ModelE Calibrated Physics Ensemble (CPE)
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
code_availability: GISS Model (version E3) atmosphere forcing data and atmosphere code are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15171581 (Elsaesser, 2025). The penalty scores and parameter data for the full PPE and CPEs are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13765601 (Elsaesser, 2024).
testbed_rationale: Provides a 45-parameter perturbed parameter ensemble and calibrated physics ensemble simulation benchmark with public data on Zenodo, suitable for training and benchmarking Earth system model surrogate models and Bayesian parameter estimation algorithms.
pain_points: High dimensionality (45 parameters) makes standard Latin Hypercube sampling sparse, requiring iterative calibrate-emulate-sample workflows.
Observational product discrepancy across independent satellite retrievals significantly alters the posterior distribution of calibrated parameters if unaddressed.
Compensating model errors can produce good cloud radiative forcing for the wrong physical reasons, necessitating simultaneous constraints across numerous cloud, environment, and radiative metrics.
Linear parameter-metric correlation screening in PPEs can wrongly classify parameters as unimportant due to strong non-linear interactions and state-dependent effects.
Host model structural deficiencies push posterior parameter estimates against prior boundary limits.
extraction_notes: The ML emulator predicts performance penalty metrics directly (which already incorporate observational discrepancies) from 45 atmospheric physics parameters, rather than predicting raw 3D atmospheric states directly. An ensemble of 6 neural networks with varied hyperparameters is averaged to mitigate overfitting and random emulator errors.
